title: Altinn Studio — Gateway
description: The runtime gateway (service gateway) in every service owner's runtime cluster: the API Designer uses to deploy apps and read their metrics, Grafana's alert webhook, and the Flux webhook that reports deploy outcomes back to Designer. Requests, deploys, Azure Monitor queries and outgoing calls come from its metrics (altinn-studio-metrics), with links to matching traces; below them, for triage, lists of failed and slow requests and of deploy events from its spans through altinn-studio-traces-logsql (LogsQL). The gateway marks every trace to be kept, so the lists are complete. Filter by environment (deployment.environment.name) and service owner (altinn.service_owner, which the runtime's collector adds to everything from a service owner's cluster). Datasource UIDs are pinned, matching the other Altinn Studio dashboards. Rates use increase_pure() over $__rate_interval divided by its length rather than rate(), so that a new series' first sample counts; deploy events are counted per interval. Instance markers come from altinn.workload.start_time: blue marks the earliest retained start per environment and version over 90 days, orange marks each process start in range (off by default, switch on Process starts).

list.name: Deploys (first start of version)
list.textFormat: {{deployment.environment.name}}. Earliest start of a process with this version in the range, in the selected service owners' clusters. A version that was already running in the hour before the range has no dot, so a rollback to it has none either.

list.name: Process starts
list.textFormat: {{deployment.environment.name}} · {{altinn.service_owner}} · {{service.version}} · {{service.instance.id}} · pod {{k8s.pod.uid}}. Includes rollout, restart and scale-up; telemetry cannot distinguish their cause.

list.name: env
list.label: Environment
list.description: Runtime environment the gateway runs in (deployment.environment.name).

list.name: service_owner
list.label: Service owner
list.description: Service owner whose runtime cluster the gateway runs in (altinn.service_owner).

list.name: filters
list.label: Filters
list.description: Filters the trace tables (LogsQL) on any span field, such as span_attr:altinn.app or span_attr:altinn.app_deploy.build.id. The metric panels have no such labels and are not filtered.

panels.title: Gateways reporting
panels.description: Gateway processes with at least one start-time sample (altinn.workload.start_time) in the preceding minute, evaluated at the range end, per environment. Each service owner's cluster runs its own gateway, usually two replicas. Counts processes exporting telemetry, not Kubernetes readiness; a replaced process remains for up to a minute.

panels.title: Versions
panels.description: The gateway versions (service.version, the commit the image was built from) running at the range end, by environment, with how many service owners' clusters and processes run each. The gateway rolls out through the runtime's release rings, so during a rollout an environment shows two versions.

panels.title: Requests per second
panels.description: Requests to the gateway's API from Designer and from Grafana's alerts, from its HTTP server metrics (http.server.request.duration). Health checks and the Flux webhook are not counted; Flux events are under Deploys.

panels.title: Server errors
panels.description: Share of API requests that failed with a 5xx. Client errors (4xx), including failed authentication, are in Client and server errors by status code.

panels.title: p95 latency
panels.description: 95th percentile duration of API requests. Most of it is calls to the Kubernetes API and Azure Monitor queries: see Azure Monitor queries and Outgoing calls below.

panels.title: Rejected credentials
panels.description: API requests per second answered 401 or 403: a Maskinporten token from Designer, or Grafana's token for alerts, that the gateway did not accept. A rise usually means a credential rotated on one side only.

panels.title: Requests in flight
panels.description: Requests the gateway is handling at the range end (http.server.active_requests), the Flux webhook's included.

panels.title: Responses by status class
panels.description: API requests per second by status class, one line per class (not stacked). Select a series to search the traces in that class; the gateway keeps every trace.

panels.title: Client and server errors by status code
panels.description: API requests per second that ended in a 4xx or 5xx, by status code. A 404 from the deploy endpoints is usually an app that is not deployed in this environment.

panels.title: Latency
panels.description: Duration of API requests: median, 95th and 99th percentile. Select a series to search traces over 1 s.

panels.title: Routes
panels.description: Every API route and method over the dashboard's time range (GET /alerts is Designer reading the alert rules, POST /alerts Grafana's alerts): requests, server errors (5xx) and their share, and the median and 95th percentile duration. (none) is requests that matched no endpoint. Sorted by requests; select a route to search its traces, or its server errors to search its failed traces.

panels.title: Service owners
panels.description: API requests and server errors (5xx), and deploy events in total and not passed on, per service owner's gateway over the time range. Sorted by server errors. (none) is a gateway whose telemetry has no altinn.service_owner, which the runtime's collector adds.

panels.title: Deploy events by reason
panels.description: Flux's install, upgrade and uninstall events for apps (altinn.gateway.deploy_events), by reason, counted per interval. The gateway passes each on to the Studio environment that deployed the app. Other Flux events are ignored and not counted.

panels.title: Deploy events not passed on
panels.description: Deploy events the gateway could not pass on to Designer, by error.type: helm_release_unresolved when the HelmRelease names no app, an HTTP status code when Designer answered with an error, or the exception type, such as a timeout. Designer then never learns the deploy's outcome. Select a series to search the traces.

panels.title: Reconcile requests by status code
panels.description: Designer's requests to reconcile an app after its deploy pipeline, counted per interval by status code. The gateway asks Flux to fetch the app's new configuration, or the whole sync root for a new app or an undeploy.

panels.title: Queries by kind
panels.description: Log Analytics queries per second for the metrics, reports and alerts Designer shows, by kind (altinn.gateway.azure_monitor.query), from altinn.gateway.azure_monitor.query.duration.

panels.title: Query duration (p95)
panels.description: 95th percentile duration of Log Analytics queries by kind. Buckets end at 120 s.

panels.title: Failed queries
panels.description: Log Analytics queries per second that failed, by kind and error.type, such as Azure.Identity.CredentialUnavailableException when the gateway has no Azure credentials, or Azure.RequestFailedException. The activity endpoints still answer 200 and report the data as unavailable; the others answer 500. Select a series to search the traces.

panels.title: Outgoing calls by host
panels.description: HTTP calls per second from the gateway by host (server.address): the Kubernetes API, Designer in each Studio environment, Log Analytics, Grafana and Maskinporten, from the HTTP client metrics (http.client.request.duration). The telemetry export to the collector is left out.

panels.title: Outgoing call latency (p95)
panels.description: 95th percentile duration of outgoing HTTP calls by host.

panels.title: Failed outgoing calls by host
panels.description: Outgoing HTTP calls per second that failed with a 5xx or without a response, by host and error.type (the status code, or the exception type, such as a timeout). 4xx responses are left out: a 404 from the Kubernetes API is an app that is not deployed. Select a series to search the failed calls' traces.

panels.title: Failed requests (traces)
panels.description: Failed gateway requests per second, counted from server spans with status error: a 5xx, an unhandled exception, or a Flux event Designer did not get, which still answers 200. Each dot is an example trace to open.

panels.title: Failures by request and error type
panels.description: Failed spans over the time range, by span name and error.type: the gateway's requests and its own spans, such as AzureMonitorClient.Query for a failed Log Analytics query and FluxWebhook.ProcessEvent for a deploy event Designer did not get.

targets.expr: {resource_attr:service.name="gateway"} "resource_attr:deployment.environment.name":in($env) "resource_attr:altinn.service_owner":~"^(${service_owner:regex})$" (kind:1 or kind:2 or kind:5) status_code:2 | stats by (name, "span_attr:error.type") count() failures, count_uniq("resource_attr:altinn.service_owner") service_owners

panels.title: Recent failed requests
panels.description: The latest 200 failed spans of the gateway: requests with status error, which ASP.NET Core sets on a 5xx or an unhandled exception, and the gateway's own failed spans. 4xx responses are not errors. Failed outgoing calls are in Alerts and outgoing calls. The gateway marks every trace it takes part in to be kept, so these lists are complete. Select a trace ID to open the trace.

targets.expr: {resource_attr:service.name="gateway"} "resource_attr:deployment.environment.name":in($env) "resource_attr:altinn.service_owner":~"^(${service_owner:regex})$" (kind:1 or kind:2 or kind:5) status_code:2 | sort by (_time desc) limit 200 | fields _time, name, "span_attr:http.response.status_code", "span_attr:error.type", "resource_attr:altinn.service_owner", "span_attr:altinn.app", "span_attr:altinn.gateway.origin_environment", duration, trace_id | rename trace_id as trace

panels.title: Recent deploy events
panels.description: The latest 200 Flux deploy events the gateway received, from the webhook's span, with the app, the Studio environment that deployed it, the Azure DevOps build (altinn.app_deploy.build.id) and, when Designer did not get the event, the error type. The trace is the webhook's own; Deploy traces below opens the deploy's. The gateway marks every trace it takes part in to be kept, so these lists are complete. Select a trace ID to open the trace.

targets.expr: {resource_attr:service.name="gateway"} "resource_attr:deployment.environment.name":in($env) "resource_attr:altinn.service_owner":~"^(${service_owner:regex})$" kind:2 "span_attr:altinn.gateway.flux.reason":* | sort by (_time desc) limit 200 | fields _time, "span_attr:altinn.gateway.flux.reason", "resource_attr:altinn.service_owner", "span_attr:altinn.app", "span_attr:altinn.gateway.origin_environment", "span_attr:altinn.app_deploy.build.id", "span_attr:error.type", duration, trace_id | rename trace_id as trace

panels.title: Deploy traces
panels.description: The gateway's part of the latest 200 deploys that carry trace context: its span in the deploy's own trace, which Designer started when the deploy was queued. Open the trace to follow the deploy from Designer through the pipeline to Flux and back. The gateway marks every trace it takes part in to be kept, so these lists are complete. Select a trace ID to open the trace.

targets.expr: {resource_attr:service.name="gateway"} "resource_attr:deployment.environment.name":in($env) "resource_attr:altinn.service_owner":~"^(${service_owner:regex})$" name:"FluxWebhook.ProcessEvent" | sort by (_time desc) limit 200 | fields _time, "span_attr:altinn.gateway.flux.reason", "resource_attr:altinn.service_owner", "span_attr:altinn.app", "span_attr:altinn.gateway.origin_environment", "span_attr:altinn.app_deploy.build.id", "span_attr:error.type", duration, trace_id | rename trace_id as trace

panels.title: Slowest requests
panels.description: The 200 slowest server spans over 1 s in the time range. Their Log Analytics queries and Kubernetes API calls are child spans in the trace. The gateway marks every trace it takes part in to be kept, so these lists are complete. Select a trace ID to open the trace.

targets.expr: {resource_attr:service.name="gateway"} "resource_attr:deployment.environment.name":in($env) "resource_attr:altinn.service_owner":~"^(${service_owner:regex})$" kind:2 duration:>1s | sort by (duration desc) limit 200 | fields _time, name, "span_attr:http.response.status_code", "resource_attr:altinn.service_owner", "span_attr:altinn.app", "span_attr:altinn.gateway.origin_environment", duration, trace_id | rename trace_id as trace

panels.title: Alerts from Grafana by rule
panels.description: Grafana's alert notifications over the time range, by alert rule (altinn.gateway.alert.rule_id), status and error type. The gateway passes each on to the Studio environment the alert names. A notification rejected before the gateway knows its rule, such as one with no alerts, has no rule here; it is in Routes as POST /alerts with a 400.

panels.title: Recent failed outgoing calls
panels.description: The latest 200 outgoing HTTP calls from the gateway that failed with a 5xx or without a response (Status empty, error.type the exception type), to the Kubernetes API, Designer, Log Analytics, Grafana and others. 4xx responses are left out: the HTTP client marks them as errors, but the gateway handles most of them, such as a 404 from the Kubernetes API for an app that isn't deployed. The gateway marks every trace it takes part in to be kept, so these lists are complete. Select a trace ID to open the trace.

targets.expr: {resource_attr:service.name="gateway"} "resource_attr:deployment.environment.name":in($env) "resource_attr:altinn.service_owner":~"^(${service_owner:regex})$" kind:3 status_code:2 !"span_attr:http.response.status_code":4* | sort by (_time desc) limit 200 | fields _time, "span_attr:http.request.method", "span_attr:server.address", "span_attr:url.full", "span_attr:http.response.status_code", "span_attr:error.type", "resource_attr:altinn.service_owner", duration, trace_id | rename trace_id as trace

panels.title: Warning and error logs
panels.description: The gateway's log records at Warning and above, the only ones it exports (from altinn-studio-logs), newest first, such as a deploy event Designer didn't get, a HelmRelease without the labels the gateway needs, or a rejected token. A record written during a request carries its trace ID: open the record and select the trace link.
